issues.detail: The Greek 'αελαβετε' (anelabete) is an aorist active indicative, implying 'you took up', 'you received', or 'you assumed'. The Vietnamese 'đã mang lấy' (already took/carried) is acceptable, but the Greek 'σκηνην του μολοχ' refers to Moloch's 'tent' or 'tabernacle'. While 'đền tạm' (tabernacle/temporary temple) is a common theological rendering, it slightly shifts the imagery from a portable tent to a building structure.

The Greek text says 'και μετοικιω υμας επεκεινα βαβυλωνος' (and I will deport/relocate you beyond Babylon). The Vietnamese 'ta sẽ đày các ngươi' uses 'đày' (exile/banish), which captures the sense of deportation but misses the specific nuance of 'μετοικιω' (to relocate/re-settle/deport to a new home).
